items.text: a roll of clean bandages
the hospital's only working measuring stick
a basket of freshly washed cloths
the inventory ledger
a very important wooden spoon used for mixing harmless salves
an aching knee
a sore shoulder
a persistent cough that warrants assessment
a headache that has already improved
the fact that nobody listens when (elder.he/she) says the benches are awful
The missing item is found exactly where it belongs. The apprentice looks personally betrayed by the shelf.
The healer creates a clear labeling system. The entire hospital suddenly seems less chaotic.
A stack of empty baskets falls over. The noise wakes the baby. Everyone freezes.
The apprentice finds the item and earns a quiet word of praise.
The apprentice admits (apprentice.he/she) moved it to "somewhere safe" and has forgotten where that is.
The apprentice asks for help rather than pretending to know. The healer is impressed.
The elder suggests a simple repair to the waiting bench. The healer thanks (elder.him/her).
The elder offers a long story about how hospitals used to work. Some of it is useful. Much of it is not.
The elder declares the hospital's decor depressing and offers to carve a cheerful wooden sign.
The parent asks for a quiet corner to feed the baby. The staff make room without treating the request as a nuisance.
The parent says (parent.he/she) would simply like to sit down. A villager immediately offers a seat.
The parent jokes that the baby has better organizational skills than the entire hospital. The healer cannot argue.
The healer discovers that the missing inventory ledger was under (healer.his/her) own arm all along.
A child wanders in carrying the missing spoon, asking why everyone is looking for the "tiny paddle."
The elder's carved sign reads "HOSPITAL: PLEASE REMAIN ALIVE." The healer requests a revision.
The baby laughs for the first time all afternoon. Every exhausted adult in the room smiles.
Nothing else goes wrong. The healer finds this suspicious.
The hospital returns to its usual routine. The healer finally sits down for a moment.
The apprentice writes a new inventory list in enormous letters so nobody can possibly miss it.
The elder leaves satisfied that somebody listened.
The parent thanks the staff and carries the baby home.
The healer says, "Tomorrow will be quieter." Nobody believes it.

intro.name: A busy day
intro.text:
The hospital is unusually busy. Nobody is in immediate danger, but everything that can go wrong seems determined to do so.
A healer, (Healer), is trying to organize supplies. A young apprentice, (Apprentice), has misplaced {A}. Meanwhile, a parent holding a sleepy infant is waiting for a routine consultation, and an elderly villager has come in to complain about {B}.

question.name: First things first
question.text: The healer has to decide what to address first.

choices.label: ASK THE APPRENTICE TO LEAD THE SEARCH.
INVITE THE ELDER TO HELP IMPROVE THE WAITING AREA.
ASK THE PARENT WHAT WOULD MAKE THE WAIT EASIER.
